newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on oversold signals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on oversold signals.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher on short covering tied to signals the market was oversold for the short term, traders said.
Commercial buying also contributed support, they said.
The higher close came about despite confirmation over the weekend that Egypt and India bought wheat from France and Australia respectively, traders said.

Egypt over the weekend bought 450,000 tonnes of French wheat and India bought 125,000 tonnes of wheat from Australia, trade and export sources said. The business with Egypt and India was factored into Friday's market, they said.

Wheat plummeted Friday to new lows in the March and May contracts on massive fund selling, estimated at roughly 27 million bushels. Fundamental traders cited the upcoming Egyptian and Indian purchases as rationale for the slide.

May early Monday dropped to a new low of $3.45-1/2 per bushel, below the previous low of $3.47 which was set Friday. March touched a session low early of $3.57, which also is its contract low and also was set Friday.
Wheat closed 1-3/4 cents per bushel higher to 1/2 lower, with March up 1-3/4 at $3.61-1/2.
The market retains the potential for volatility, traders pointed out.
They cited Friday's Commodity Futures Trading Commission Commitments of Traders report showed funds, as of January 28, were short wheat by 66.820 million bushels and long by 38.73 million bushels.
Also CFTC said commercials were short 135.280 million bushels and long by 108.835 million bushels.
That scenario plus short term relative strength indexes (RSI) indicating the market was oversold, could lead to short covering rallies, traders said.

The nine-day RSI for March reached 20 percent early Monday and closed at 27 percent, below the 30 percent level which is generally considered by chartists as indicative of a market nearing oversold status.
Technicians cited first support in the March at $3.54-1/2 and second support at $3.41-1/2. The session low for March was $3.57 per bushel which is the contract low that was set Friday.
First resistance in the March was $3.67-1/2 and second resistance was at $3.80-1/2. The session high for March was $3.63 per bushel.

The market also gained mild bullish input from Monday's USDA weekly export inspections report. USDA said U.S. wheat inspected for export during the week ended January 30 totaled 16.724 million bushels, above expectations for seven to 11 million bushels.
"There were no real surprises, maybe the wheat number was a little constructive," Cermak said.
News also circulated that Taiwan would be in the market overnight for 50,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat.

"There was a little commercial buying," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co. Traders said Cargill Inc bought three million bushels of March in early dealings and was a late buyer of one-half million bushels each of March and May.
"There's just nothing bullish today in these markets," a trader said.

There was news early Monday that India's wheat output in 1996-97 (July-June) is expected to be around 65 million tonnes, compared with 62.6 million last year. Statistics Canada early Monday said as of December 31 Canadian wheat stocks totaled 19.108 million tonnes, above the year earlier tally of 14.755 million tonnes.
Also grain merchandisers said Monday that cash basis bids for hard red winter wheat were lower Monday in response to a recent increase in farmer selling.
Traders agreed fundamentals remain bearish.
Technicians also said the key four and 20-day moving averages early Monday continued to give off bearish warning flags.

In addition to the Cargill buying of the March contract, Dean Witter bought 1.5 million March, ADM Investor Services sold two million March and FIMAT Futures sold two million July and sold one million March, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 19,000 contracts, below the 27,370 traded Friday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, FIMAT Futures bought 2,200 May $3.60 puts and sold 2,200 May $3.50 puts at 6-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, slightly below the 8,268 traded Friday.
